There are some ulama that are of the opinion that this type of banking and the services that they provide are halaal and a practicing Muslim should have not fear and fully take advantage of the variety of services being offered by these same banks. On the other hand there are a group of scholars that aver that this type of banking is no different than regular commercial non Islamic banks. The only differences being in the terminology, but the actual transactions fall into the category of riba. Our question to the ulama ikram is: in the opinion of your darul iftaa, which group is correct, as both can not be correct in this case. answer: Transactions & Dealings >> Other Transactions Question ID: 37246 Country: India Title: Rent received is haram or halal. Question: I have a commercial office. A sports bar company has approached me to take my office on rent (Galaxy Entertainment Corporation Ltd - Mumbai ). The nature of their business is , they have big restaurants and other large spaces, in other areas outside my office premises, where people come to play different types of games and at the same time they relax and drink alcohol. Now the point is that they are not carrying out any of their business activities in my office such as playing of games or serving alcohol. They are just going to manage their accounts and administration in my office. My question is that is this rent that I shall receive - Halal or Haram. Please reply most urgently as I have to reply to them in 3 to 4 days. Answer ID: 37246 Posted on: Aug 30, 2020 Bismillah hir-Rahman nir-Rahim ! (Fatwa: 411/162/L=1433) If they only will manage their accounts and administatration in your office, then you can give your office to them on rent. And thus you will be permitted to use the amount of rent paid by them. Allah (Subhana Wa Ta'ala) knows Best Darul Ifta, Darul Uloom Deoband, India
